content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008\", \"title\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\", \"name\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\", \"revisionId\": \"5ddbee1c86\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-30T16:25:41Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-30T16:58:19Z\", \"text\": \"ZM3D playable: hand-off notes\\n\\nThe brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.\\n\\nThe hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.\\n\\nState is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.\\n\\nBrian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.\\n\\nSound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.\\n\\nTickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.\\n\\nSharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_8c1d0bca1d1d5fde4c5008", "title": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "name": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes", "revisionId": "5ddbee1c86", "createdTime": "2025-09-30T16:25:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-30T16:58:19Z", "text": "ZM3D playable: hand-off notes

The brief. One doc PlayableX can build from: which scenario we picked and what it is for, the eight items on the board and that every other board item on the list is an extra they can swap in, the four zombies and the one animation, how a level is won and lost and how many slots the tray has, what they can use for sound and when the music may start, and the start date. How the level plays is on the design page; your deck of the reference level has what we built for them. What they told us about formats still holds, and so does their rule from last time about when the music may start.

The hand-off list. One row per line of Brian's pack list, with these columns: Line, Category, Board set, State, What's owed, Who has it, Ticket. Line, Category and Ticket are as on his list. Board set is Default for the eight on the board and Extra for every other board item; leave it empty for anything that isn't a board item.

State is one of three words, nothing else. Delivered: PlayableX has the current file and can use it. Ready: exported in a format they take and sitting in the outgoing folder, it opens, it is the current version and nobody is changing it. Owed: anything else. For an Owed line say what is owed, and who has it, meaning whoever has to do the next thing.

Brian's note on each ticket says what he did with the line. Take it as it stands unless something later says otherwise, and go by how things stand today, not the day he wrote it: if someone who knows the file or the art has said something since, that counts. If the art changed after a file went out or was exported (a fix, a retexture, new colour versions), it goes again, and it sits with whoever the file came from.

Sound: we only hand over what is ours to hand over. Anything from a library or a bought pack stays here until we have our own version.

Tickets live under Brian's pack ticket, one per line. An Owed line's ticket goes to Todo with a comment saying what is owed and who has it. Leave the Delivered and Ready ones as they are.

Sharing: both files, view only. Everyone on the kickoff hold, and PlayableX through their intake address, which is in Contacts.
"}

I'm 99% certain that we have quite significant number of bots.\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1759207989.371869\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759189466.554739\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID> Got new colored version of cactus, chainsaw and cones that can probably come in handy:\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759176983.189479\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I think we should think about what 0.3.22 had and what we're keeping.\\n\\u2022 Blunder was fine the way it is, but it got skewed because of these recent weird bot like behavior.\\n\\u2022 Win rate still has more impact on funnel, blunder seems to be OK as long as people win.\\n\\u2022 We are leaning more hardcore because casual doesn't cut it, or so we think\\n\\u2022 We support this hardcore transition with level templates and monster scaling using a math formula\\n\\u2022 We differentiate our game with the zombie killing + card mechanic\\n\\u2022 Our live ops are fine since leaderboards/quests are standard in all RPGs. My understanding is that hardcore players in general are totally OK with being challenged more on the reflex side of things. \\n\\u2022 Hardcore players are also more tolerant of deeper systems like item stats and monster stats.\\n\\u2022 The only downside is if we were to lean into something more hardcore, development cost goes up the more systems we try to introduce.\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1759176983.189479\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759173778.362129\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Very well, in that case, from now on if someone complains a level is \\\"too hard\\\" I'll just ignore them :smile:\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1759173778.362129\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759173703.509829\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"If we can go with zombie scaling then I agree wth levels being mid core or not casual\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0012_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759173698.236239\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"For one thing we'd make the levels so that they would have deck building blocks and not put the baseline at CPM and win streak free win.\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1759173698.236239\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759173693.774649\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"But given the current situation, since we\\u2019re not getting good performance from a casual game, I assume we\\u2019re considering shifting towards a more hardcore game as an alternative\", \"channel\": \"C090N54TG79\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759173684.934029\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Personally, I\\u2019ve never supported a hardcore match-3D game. • In Archero 2, the Arena usually uses a fixed set of monster types. These monsters are presented to the player in different sequences, creating variation across levels. I believe the game also adjusts level design based on the player’s current power-ups or skills. For example, if your build makes you stronger while standing still, you’re more likely to face levels that force you to move and kite enemies. Still, most levels seem to follow certain predefined monster patterns.
    ◦ Another thing I’m confident about is that the monsters’ HP, defense, and attack stats increase as you progress. A monster you encounter at Level 1 will appear again at Level 45, but with boosted stats. This scaling seems to be the game’s way of balancing the player’s increasing strength.
• In <http://Survivor.io|Survivor.io>, I don’t think monsters’ individual stats scale the same way. Instead, the difficulty comes from changes in camera zoom, monster variety, and, most importantly, quantity. The pool of monster types stays fairly limited, but the numbers ramp up dramatically. For instance, the same type of monster that spawns at the 0-minute mark might still appear at 6 minutes, but instead of 10 showing up, you’re suddenly dealing with 100. {"result":"{\"id\": \"page_zm3d_gdd\", \"space_id\": \"space_PROD\", \"parent_id\": \"page_prod_home\", \"title\": \"Zombie Match 3D \\u2014 Game Design Document\", \"body\": \"

This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (shipped on the store as Puzzles vs Zombies under Calm Play LLC until the transfer to Harmony Games and the rename on 24 July 2025). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design - Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass - Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs - 2025 H1.

ZM3D has not had a global launch. It first became publicly downloadable in the US on Google Play on April 12, 2025 and on the App Store on April 18, 2025; May 15, 2025 is the day iOS build 1.0.5 went live. This GDD reflects that build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match it counts as a blunder: the tray clears and surviving monsters enrage, but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state - the loss screen only appears at zero health. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics - objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray - the primary tempo penalty, not the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families - cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

The roster is an everyday-people theme rather than classic undead. Minion families scale in tiers; bosses come in standard, Fast and Turbo variants.

FamilyTypeTiers
PunkMinion1-5
BikerMinion1-4
KarenMinion1-4
AfroMinion1-3
Riot Police, Chef, Scientist, Fire Fighter, Magician, Librarian, Tech Bro, Gym Bro, Baseball Player, CheerleaderMinionin development
VarC-Mayor1 250 / VarC-Mayor2 225 / VarC-Chef 175 (base HP, scaled at runtime; the older 180/300/500 prefabs are retired)Bossstandard, Fast, Turbo

Elemental weaknesses used by boosters and abilities: shock, poison, burn, freeze, splash, stun, blind. Glue is a booster, not an element.

Modes

  • Campaign - authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless - survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss - a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, reached production in the week of September 22-29, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc - do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash from consecutive glass-impact SFX/VFX on Android, mostly Samsung (Aug-Sep 2025, ZOM-475), fixed by removing the glass SFX and VFX. The separate addressables splash-hang belongs to Domino Delights.
  • The font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections is also Domino Delights (ENG-2346, May 2025); the ZM3D client has no remote font download.

Boss mode reward config

Owner: Robert (Product). Design: Julia Lawson. Changes to tray count or refill cadence must be reviewed against the OKR dashboard before shipping.

==== Mon, 24 Jul 2023 21:35:17 -0700 robert <robert@harmonygames.co> | Re: [SOURCE_ORG_0001] <> Jonathan Sprint Planning Help
Hi PERSON_3127_NAME,

Nice to meet you! I think for the most part I'm just a sprint planning
noob. I've attended a handful of them in the last 10 years but usually they
don't invite the marketing folks so I don't remember much. I think as
Leonard mentioned, what we really want to do is distill our product roadmap
into the small bite size pieces and milestones so we can efficiently tackle
them and deliver them on time.

We want to start with using tools like Trello + Linear but we're open to
anything.

I have also CC'ed our game design lead [PERSON_NAME_0043], who just joined us last
week and will be part of this pr[USERNAME_37405].

How does Thursday 11 AM look like for you? If it's open I'll send an invite
over.

Thanks!

[PERSON_NAME_0054]

On Mon, Jul 24, 2023 at 8:18 PM PERSON_3127_NAME <PERSON_3127_EMAIL>
wrote:

> Hey Leonard,
>
> Awesome to e-meet you [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake!
>
> Sorry for the slow reply, this email seemed to have gotten caught in a
> spam folder (fixed it so this shouldn't happen again).
>
> Thanks for all these amazing details this gives me a solid understanding
> of what you all are aiming to do and the what value you see production
> adding to your team.
>
> Happy to chat further, I’m available anytime this Wednesday-Friday from
> 9am-6pm pst.
>
> I’d definitely also like to hear from [PERSON_NAME_0054], Blake, and anyone else you
> think relevant on what production gaps they may be anticipating and/or
> areas they may want a producer to add value.
>
>
>
> On Wed, Jul 19, 2023 at 4:58 PM Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>
> wrote:
>
>> Hi PERSON_3127_NAME,
>>
>> Thank you again for your time last week. I wanted to share with you some
>> material to help you prepare for our next meeting where you will meet my
>> co-founders (please meet [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Blake, they are [MISC_0251]) and help us
>> understand how to set ourselves up for success with proper sprint planning.
>>
>> *Gameplay*
>> First and foremost we have 2 strong reference games.
>>
>> We are closest to Domino Dreams:
>> https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/domino-dreams/id6444043291
>> Our next closest and biggest competitor is Grand Harvest Solitaire:
>> https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/solitaire-grand-harvest/id1223338261
>>
>> Domino Dreams is still in beta and has promising metrics. Grand
>> Harvest Solitaire has been around for a while and they made about $650M net
>> revenue globally over the last 4 years and are on track to be a $1B+ game.
>>
>> *
==== Tue, 25 Jul 2023 08:33:32 -0700 PERSON_3127_NAME <PERSON_3127_EMAIL> | Re: [SOURCE_ORG_0001] <> Jonathan Sprint Planning Help
11am on Thursday works great [PERSON_NAME_0054]. Happy to talk through some high level

input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (Puzzles vs Zombies). Written 1 Oct 2025 by Julia Lawson for the game as it is today. If our core gameplay changes, we will redo the affected parts with you in November.

1. Start date
Kickoff with PlayableX: Monday 3 November 2025. The project is paused until then.

2. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1: the core gameplay, shown simply. The playable is meant to filter for retention. It should show players the real game, so the ones who install are the ones who will like it, while still being fun. It is not meant to chase the cheapest CPI with something unrelated to the game. Presenting the core mechanic in its simplest form is what you recommended too.

3. How the level plays (from our design doc)
- Items sit in a 3D physics pile. The player taps or drags items into a tray at the bottom.
- The tray has 7 slots. Three matching items in the tray clear, and each cleared triple fires that item at the zombies.
- Different items hit zombies differently: for example, Grenade is powerful, Couch does splash damage, and Plushie Chick is weak but funny.
- Zombies walk toward the player. When they reach the player they drain the player's HP.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach the player and HP runs out.
- Filling all 7 slots without a match is not a loss. It is a blunder: the tray clears, the surviving zombies enrage, and play continues. Only zero HP shows the lose screen.
- The rocket launcher (our Cannon, sent with its projectile) is the weapon on screen.
Reference: our deck "ZM3D playable - reference level" (built 23 Sep, recorded by Brian) shows the level we built for you. Note that its board had Couch and Pillow and Plushie Bunny; under this brief those two are extras, and the default eight are listed below.

4. The board: eight default items
Grenade, Couch, Plushie Chick (the one you called the duck), Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant, Dynamite.
Every other board item on our pack list is an extra you can swap in (you offered to make the board editable). The hand-off list marks each board item Default or Extra.
Still owed for the default eight: Cactus Plant, which has new pot colour versions coming from Claire. The other seven are already with you or ready in the outgoing folder.

5. Zombies and animation
Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player.
One animation: walk.
All four are in the Unity package Marcus sent on 26 Sep, which you have already reviewed. Please re-rig just these four in Spine with the walk animation only. We can add more zombies later if size allows.

6. Sound and music
What you can use, all as .wav:
- Ours and ready now: Matching sound, Success sound, Failure sound.
- Background music: a new track made for the ad (not the in-game track). Calvin is still cutting it down to a loop, and it will follow.
- Rocket sound and Explosion sound: the current versions come from a sound library and a bought pack, so we are not handing them over. We will send our own versions when Calvin has made them. Until then, leave those cues silent or use placeholders on your side.
Music start rule (yours, from the Domino Delights playable): music starts only after the player's first tap, never on load. The same goes for the timer: it must not start before the player can see the playable.

7. Formats (as you told us, still holds)
- 3D: .fbx (Binary, not ASCII), .glb or .blend
- 2D: .png (2D animation parts separated)
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

8. What is still coming from us
See the hand-off list (sheet "ZM3D playable - hand-off list"). It has one row per line of our pack list, each marked Delivered (you have it), Ready (exported and in our outgoing folder) or Owed (still to do, with what is owed and who has it). Counts as of 1 Oct: 8 Delivered, 48 Ready, 40 Owed.

• **Delivered: 8**: Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, Zombie characters (Marcus's pack)
• **Ready: 48**
• **Owed: 40**

Where Brian's notes no longer hold:
• **Bathroom (12)**: Claire said on 29 Sep she's redoing the UVs and that Friday's files are the old version. They go again from her.

• **8 music instruments**: per Brian's note on 30 Sep, the zip got cut off on upload and they aren't in the folder. Brian will put them back.
• **Rocket and Explosion sounds**: these are from Soundly and an Asset Store pack, so they stay with us until Calvin makes our own versions.

The rest of Owed: Claire 6 models not exported yet, Brian 5 exports plus 2 Figma PNG lines, Calvin the music loop, Martin the fonts. All 40 Owed tickets are in Todo with a comment. Robert's picks stand: walk, plus Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player.
